rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (kd 1.2) is the best design so far at 495.2. The oval finishes 20/20 at 1.77 s with max_error 0.019 and 0.6 line-loss events. The s-bend finishes 5/20 with progress 0.84, and the slalom is 0/20 with progress 0.15. Steering oscillation stays near 0.19 on the oval, so the robot is not ringing. Failures are outward excursions past the 0.06 m off-track limit on sharp alternating bends, and body width is already at its maximum.

Trend in the single-variable kd changes at fixed geometry and gains: kd 0.8 gave s-bend progress 0.46 (iter 3); kd 1.0 with sensors moved to y=0.06 gave 0.61 (iter 7); kd 1.2 gave 0.84 (iter 8). Oval steering oscillation fell from 0.197 to 0.189 over the same change, so the extra damping has not added jitter. Slalom progress also rose monotonically (0.09, 0.12, 0.15). Earlier attempts that changed kp, base_speed, wheel_track or sensor span all reduced oval reliability, so I leave them fixed.

Change: kd 1.2 to 1.4, nothing else. Geometry and controller are otherwise identical to iteration 8. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.9 with more finishes, slalom progress around 0.18 to 0.2, oval still 20/20 at about 1.75 s, and steering_oscillation near or below 0.2. Risk: higher kd may amplify sensor noise. If oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3 or oval completion drops below 1.0, revert to kd 1.2. Hypotheses: (H1) derivative damping is still the limiting factor on alternating bends, so more kd keeps improving s-bend and slalom progress. (H2) Once kd passes about 1.4, the gain shows diminishing returns, and slalom survival will need a lower base_speed or a different line_loss mode. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and oval completion_time.
